tldr: CRISPR-GPT is an LLM agent augmented with domain knowledge and external computational tools that automates and enhances the design process of CRISPR-based gene-editing experiments, addressing the hallucinations and domain gaps of general-purpose LLMs.
contributions: Introduction of CRISPR-GPT, an LLM agent that combines domain knowledge with external tools for automated CRISPR experimental design
Four-module architecture (LLM planner, Tool provider, Task executor, LLM Agent) with 22 tasks organized as state machines
Three operational modes: Meta Mode (predefined pipelines), Auto Mode (custom task decomposition), and Q&A Mode (ad hoc queries)
Human evaluation with 12 CRISPR experts comparing against ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0
Real-world wet-lab validation of CRISPR-GPT-assisted gene knockout experiments
methods: CRISPR-GPT uses a four-module architecture where an LLM planner decomposes user requests into dependent tasks via ReAct prompting, a Tool provider wraps external APIs (guideRNA libraries, Primer3, web search) with user-friendly interfaces, a Task executor implements 22 tasks as state machines with sub-goal decomposition, and an LLM Agent acts as the user-facing intermediary making sequential decisions. The system was evaluated through human assessment by 12 CRISPR experts rating responses on a 1-5 scale and through wet-lab validation where an independent scientist used CRISPR-GPT to design and execute Cas12a-mediated knockouts of TGFBR1, SNAI1, BAX, and BCL2L1 in A375 cells via lentiviral delivery, followed by sequencing confirmation.
results: CRISPR-GPT supports multiple gene-editing scenarios including single gene knockout, base editing, prime editing, and CRISPR activation/interference. Human evaluation compared CRISPR-GPT outputs against ChatGPT 3.5 and ChatGPT 4.0 rated by 12 experts. Wet-lab validation successfully produced CRISPR-Cas12a knockouts: 4 crRNAs were cloned via Golden Gate assembly into a Cas12a backbone, lentivirus was packaged in HEK-293T cells and used to transduce A375 cells, and sequencing confirmed editing at target loci.
limitations: General-purpose LLMs hallucinate incorrect gRNA sequences with high confidence (e.g., for EMX1 and EGFR targets)
Current CRISPR-GPT version does not allow dynamic addition or deletion of new tasks during automatic execution
System restrictions prevent use in human subjects
Responses from general LLMs often lack essential experimental details and contain irrelevant information
